title: Humboldt and Bonpland through Spanish America, 1799–1804
summary: Humboldt and Bonpland sailed from A Coruña in June 1799 with a Spanish royal passport. They went up the Orinoco and through the Casiquiare Channel, over the Andes by Bogotá and Quito, up Chimborazo to some 5,878 metres in 1802, to Lima, Acapulco and Mexico City. They returned by Havana and the United States, where Humboldt met Jefferson, and reached Bordeaux in August 1804.

events.label: The Casiquiare Channel
events.text: They paddled the natural channel that joins the Orinoco to the Río Negro and so to the Amazon basin. Spanish missionaries and Indigenous people knew it; Humboldt's measurements and map made it known in Europe.

events.label: Chimborazo, about 5,878 metres
events.text: Humboldt, Bonpland and Carlos Montúfar climbed the volcano to some 5,878 metres, a record at the time, and turned back below the summit at a crevasse. The mountain's flanks became the plates of his plant geography.
